exposure: Parous women without a previous cesarean
Mode of delivery (spontaneous or operative vaginal delivery)
Women with vaginal birth after cesarean
cohort: Women with singleton pregnancies at term gestation in Canada (excluding Quebec) who had vaginal deliveries
finding: While episiotomy use has declined in Canada, it was associated with higher rates of obstetric anal sphincter injury in spontaneous vaginal deliveries but lower rates in operative vaginal deliveries, particularly forceps deliveries, among nulliparous women and those with previous cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Episiotomy was associated with lower rates of obstetric anal sphincter injury in operative vaginal deliveries, particularly forceps deliveries.
